text: The Python programming language uses indentation (whitespace) rather than braces to delimit blocks. PEP 8 recommends four spaces per indentation level. Mixing tabs and spaces raises IndentationError or TabError at compile time.
query: How does Python denote code blocks?

text: SearXNG is a privacy-respecting metasearch engine that aggregates results from engines such as DuckDuckGo, Brave, Wikipedia, and arXiv. It can expose a JSON API when search.formats includes json. Self-hosting keeps the UI private but queries still reach upstream engines.
query: What is SearXNG?

text: Qdrant is a vector database designed for similarity search over embeddings. It supports HNSW approximate nearest neighbor indexes, payload filtering, and cosine or Euclidean distance. Collections store dense vectors with optional metadata.
query: Which database stores embedding vectors?

text: Cosine similarity measures the cosine of the angle between two vectors. It is scale-invariant and widely used to compare embedding vectors for semantic search. A score of 1 means identical direction; 0 means orthogonal.
query: Metric for comparing embedding vectors?

text: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) lets LLM hosts call tools, read resources, and fetch prompts over stdio or HTTP transports. Cursor and VS Code can launch a local MCP server as a subprocess. Tools are declared with typed schemas inferred from function signatures.
query: What protocol exposes tools to LLM hosts?

text: Trafilatura is a Python library that extracts the main textual content from HTML pages while discarding navigation, ads, and boilerplate. It is commonly used after HTTP fetch in research agents. It does not execute JavaScript.
query: Library for HTML to clean text?

text: Recall at k in information retrieval measures the fraction of relevant documents that appear among the top k retrieved results. Perfect recall@k is 1.0 when every relevant item is in the top k. It ignores ranking order within those k.
query: RAG metric for top-k retrieval?

text: Mean reciprocal rank (MRR) averages the reciprocal of the rank of the first relevant document across queries. If the first relevant hit is at rank 2, that query contributes 0.5. MRR emphasizes getting a good answer early.
query: MRR definition in IR?

text: Ollama runs local large language models and embedding models and exposes an HTTP API on localhost. The /api/embed endpoint returns dense vectors. Models such as nomic-embed-text are pulled with ollama pull before use.
query: Local runner for nomic-embed-text?

text: In the open-search lab, the default memory backend stores chunk text and embedding vectors as JSON inside a SQLite file and performs a brute-force cosine scan at query time. This is simple for small corpora but is O(n) in the number of chunks.
query: Default memory backend in open-search lab?

text: DuckDuckGo is frequently configured as an upstream engine inside SearXNG for general web results. It emphasizes privacy relative to major search portals. Metasearch still depends on upstream availability and rate limits.
query: Privacy search engine in metasearch?

text: arxiv.org is a preprint server hosting papers in physics, mathematics, computer science, and related fields. Authors upload manuscripts before or instead of journal publication. SearXNG science category often includes arXiv results.
query: Where to find CS preprints?

text: HTTP status code 403 Forbidden means the server understood the request but refuses to authorize it. Unlike 401, authenticating may not help. Common causes include missing permissions, WAF rules, or hotlink protection.
query: Status code when access denied?

text: When splitting long documents into RAG chunks, overlapping windows (for example 100 characters of overlap on 1000-character chunks) helps preserve sentences that would otherwise be cut at boundaries, improving retrieval of context that spans two chunks.
query: Why overlap text chunks in RAG?

text: Text embedding models map passages and queries into dense vectors so that semantically related texts are close under cosine similarity. They enable semantic retrieval beyond keyword matching. Model choice strongly affects recall on domain corpora.
query: Purpose of embedding models?

text: The Brave Search API provides web search over Brave's independent index rather than reselling Google or Bing results. It is often chosen for privacy-conscious production agents. Pricing is typically per thousand requests.
query: API with own index not Google repack?

text: Exa (formerly Metaphor) offers neural and semantic web search APIs aimed at AI agents. It is strong at discovery and find-similar-pages tasks. Cloudflare Web Search can route to Exa as one upstream provider.
query: Semantic search provider for agents?

text: Cloudflare Web Search is an abstraction that routes agent search calls through AI Gateway to providers such as Ceramic, Exa, and Linkup with a uniform result schema. It is convenient with Workers but is not a fully local stack.
query: Cloudflare search abstraction providers?

text: JSON Lines (JSONL) stores one JSON object per line. It is convenient for streaming datasets and benchmarks because records can be appended without rewriting a whole array. The open-search benches use .jsonl query files.
query: Format for bench query files?

text: Server-side request forgery (SSRF) defenses block fetchers from requesting internal addresses such as 169.254.169.254 (cloud instance metadata) or link-local hosts. Agents that fetch user-supplied URLs must validate schemes and hosts.

HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World) graphs are a popular approximate nearest neighbor index structure. Qdrant and many vector databases use HNSW to trade a small recall loss for large speed gains versus exact scan.
query: Qdrant index algorithm family?

text: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) retrieves relevant passages from a corpus and conditions an LLM on those passages to produce grounded answers with citations. Quality depends on both retrieval metrics and faithfulness of generation.
query: Retrieval augmented generation acronym?

text: MTEB (Massive Text Embedding Benchmark) evaluates embedding models across retrieval, classification, clustering, STS, and other tasks. Public leaderboards on Hugging Face help choose models like nomic-embed-text or bge-m3.
query: Embedding model leaderboard benchmark?

text: HotpotQA is a multi-hop question answering dataset that requires combining evidence from multiple Wikipedia paragraphs. It is often used to stress-test RAG systems beyond single-passage lookup.
query: Multi-hop QA dataset name?

text: MS MARCO is a large-scale passage ranking and question answering dataset derived from Bing search logs. It is a standard IR benchmark for dense retrievers and classic BM25 baselines.
query: Passage ranking benchmark corpus?

text: Playwright drives a headless Chromium, Firefox, or WebKit browser to render JavaScript-heavy single-page apps before extraction. Use it when plain HTTP clients like httpx return empty or incomplete HTML for SPAs.
query: Tool when httpx extract fails on SPAs?

text: SearXNG organizes engines into categories such as general, science, it, and news. The open-search lab maps modes academic to science, code to it, news to news so agents can bias result types without changing backends.
query: SearXNG category for code search mode?

text: Zero data retention (ZDR) policies commit a provider not to store customer query content beyond request handling. Cloudflare markets ZDR for some Web Search paths; self-hosted SearXNG avoids third-party AI-search APIs but still queries upstream engines.
query: Privacy policy for search API logs?

text: httpx is a modern Python HTTP client supporting sync and async APIs, HTTP/2, and timeouts. The open-search fetch layer uses httpx to download pages before trafilatura extraction.
query: HTTP client used by fetch layer?

text: pytest is the standard Python test runner for unit tests. Fixtures provide setup isolation. The open-search unit tests use pytest with local fixtures and no network.
query: Test runner for metrics and fixtures?

text: Euclidean distance (L2) measures straight-line distance between points in vector space. Unlike cosine similarity, it is sensitive to vector magnitude. Some vector databases support both metrics per collection.
query: When is L2 distance preferred over cosine for vectors?

text: BM25 is a classical bag-of-words ranking function used by keyword search engines such as Elasticsearch and Lucene. It does not use neural embeddings. Hybrid RAG systems sometimes fuse BM25 hits with dense retrieval.
query: Classical keyword ranking function without neural embeddings?

text: FAISS is a Facebook AI Similarity Search library for efficient dense vector indexing and search on CPU and GPU. It is a library, not a full network database service like Qdrant or Milvus.
query: Facebook library for GPU vector similarity search?

text: Milvus is an open-source vector database for large-scale embedding search. Like Qdrant it offers ANN indexes and filtering, but the APIs and deployment model differ.
query: Open-source vector database alternative to Qdrant?

text:
asyncio is Python's standard library for concurrent I/O using an event loop.
A Task wraps a coroutine. Calling task.cancel() schedules CancelledError into the coroutine at the next await.
In Python 3.11+, TaskGroup provides structured concurrency: if one child fails, siblings are cancelled.
Never call time.sleep in async code; use await asyncio.sleep. Blocking disk or CPU work should go to asyncio.to_thread.
create_task schedules a coroutine to run concurrently; gather waits for multiple awaitables.
query: How does asyncio Task cancel interact with CancelledError?

text:
Kubernetes uses probes to decide pod health. A livenessProbe failure restarts the container.
A readinessProbe failure removes the pod from Service endpoints without restarting it.
Startup probes delay other probes for slow-starting apps. For an HTTP Go service, probe an inexpensive /healthz that does not depend on downstreams.
Behind an nginx Ingress, readiness failures stop new traffic while in-flight requests may still finish.
query: Difference between Kubernetes liveness and readiness probes?

text:
Practical RAG chunking balances context and precision. Chunks of roughly 500 to 1500 characters with 10 to 20% overlap are common.
Too-small chunks lose discourse; too-large chunks dilute embedding specificity.
Store source URL and chunk index as metadata. After retrieval, optional reranking with a cross-encoder improves precision@k.
Always re-embed the entire corpus when changing embedding models; mixing vector spaces silently destroys recall.
query: Recommended chunk size and overlap for RAG embeddings?
